title: Trump Approval at Second-Term Lows Across Multiple Polls — Silver Bulletin Net -18.9; Pew 34%; Quinnipiac 38%; Only 25% Among Independents
detail: Multiple polls released in mid-May 2026 show President Trump's approval rating at second-term lows. The Silver Bulletin aggregate (Nate Silver) shows ~36.8% approval / 59.7% disapproval, a net of -18.9 — the worst aggregate of his second term. Pew Research (April 20-26) recorded 34% approval — the lowest single poll of the second term. Quinnipiac showed 38%; CNN/SSRS 35%. Among independents, at least one poll showed just 25% approval — a stark erosion from his January 2025 inauguration numbers. Among the Republican base, approval has fallen to ~68% from a high of 95% at inauguration. Key drivers of disapproval include cost of living, national gas prices at $4.52/gallon driven by the Iran war oil shock, and the conduct of the US-Iran conflict. The poll slide comes as Trump returns from Beijing with disputed claims of trade deal breakthroughs that China has not confirmed.

media.caption: Pew Research: Trump approval at 34% — lowest of second term; erosion across personal trait assessments

title: Trump Urges Republicans to Vote Out Sen. Cassidy in Louisiana Primary — Endorses Challenger Julia Letlow
detail: On May 16, 2026 — the date of the Louisiana Republican primary — President Trump publicly called for all Republicans to vote out Sen. Bill Cassidy (R-LA), endorsing challenger Julia Letlow instead. Cassidy has been a persistent thorn for Trump allies since voting to convict Trump at the second impeachment trial in February 2021. The Louisiana primary is part of Trump's broader effort to reshape the Republican Party in his image by supporting primary challengers against any Republican who challenged him. Letlow, a congresswoman from Louisiana's 5th district, was seen as a solidly MAGA-aligned alternative.

media.caption: Trump endorses Julia Letlow against Sen. Bill Cassidy in Louisiana Republican primary

title: White House Releases 2026 US Counterterrorism Strategy — First of Trump's Second Term
detail: The Trump administration released its first counterterrorism strategy document of the second term in May 2026, published on the White House website. The 2026 US Counterterrorism Strategy outlines the administration's approach to domestic and international terrorism threats, building on lessons from the post-9/11 era and incorporating the administration's priorities around border security, Islamist extremism, and the designation of cartels as foreign terrorist organizations. The strategy release comes amid the ongoing US-Iran conflict and heightened concern about blowback threats from Iranian-aligned proxies.
